title: Unitary matrices and preserved geometry
objectives: Verify unitarity by adjoint multiplication and column inner products.
Explain preserved inner products and distinguish unitary, Hermitian and invertible.
prerequisites: Chapter 2’s vectors, basis labels and matrix multiplication; elementary algebra. New notation is developed in the text.

quizzes.question: An invertible matrix preserves the norm of one chosen input. Is it necessarily unitary?
options: No; the condition must hold for all inputs.
Yes, if that input is normalized.
feedback: An invertible scaling can preserve one direction and stretch another.
Correct. Verify U†U=I rather than one example.
Normalization of one input does not establish a property of the full operator.

quizzes.question: Which statement is correct about a rank-one projector in a two-dimensional space?
options: It is always a unitary gate.
It is Hermitian and idempotent, but not invertible on the full space.
It must preserve every vector’s norm.
feedback: Correct. These properties differ from unitarity.
